newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast spot gas firms amid refinery problem.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast spot gas firms amid refinery problem.

text.p: Wholesale spot prices for U.S. West Coast gasoline and diesel fuel edged higher Friday, amid concerns of tightened supply after a gasoline-making unit shut at Atlantic Richfield's refinery near Los Angeles.
The unit, which makes about 43,000 barrels-per-day of gasoline and diesel fuel, shut due to an unspecified problem and its return date is not yet known.
"The rumor was (ARCO) was in the market buying gas," one trader said.

Energy futures prices also rose in New York, with the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) seeing August crude oil up 11 cents a barrel to $19.33. Crude oil futures generally influence the West Coast spot markets, along with product futures.
July CARB gasoline sold to refineries in Los Angeles at 55 cents and 56 cents a gallon, traders said. Traders talked the grade between 55.50 and 56.50 cents, one cent higher than Thursday.
August barrels sold for about a penny higher than July, traders said, because of perceived excess supply this month.
CARB diesel was talked between 55 and 56 cents a gallon, a one cent increase over Thursday.

A parcel of CARB gasoline sold for 57 cents a gallon, traders said, keeping the grade about one cent over L.A. Although L.A. normally holds a one cent premium over the Bay, prices have risen in the north the last month due to higher volumes of exports.
Reformulated gasoline, for sale in the metropolitan Phoennix
area, was talked 1.50 cents below CARB levels,traders said.
